# 11QMelchizedek Column 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Consensus Arbiter) | **Source:** 11Q13 (Cave 11), Col. 2 | **Condition:** fragmentary; main surviving column with ~26 partially preserved lines

---

**2:1** [...And concerning what] He said: "In [this] year of jubilee, [each of you shall return to his property" (Lev 25:13);

**2:2** and concerning what] He said: "Eve[ry] creditor shall release [what he has lent to his neighbor; he shall not exact it of his neighbor or his brother, for]

**2:3** the release of God [has been proclaimed]" (Deut 15:2).

**2:4** [Its inter]pretation for the last days concerns the captives, about whom

**2:5** He said: "To proclaim liberty to the captives" (Isa 61:1). Its interpretation is that He will assign them to the Sons of Heaven and to the inheritance of Melchizedek,

**2:6** [for He will re]store them. And he will proclaim liberty to them, to release them from [the debt of] all their iniquities.

**2:7** And this will [take place] in the first week of the jubilee that follows the ni[ne] jubilees.

**2:8** And the Day of [Atone]ment is the e[nd of the] tenth [jub]ilee,

**2:9** when atonement shall be made for all the Sons of [Light and] for the people of the lot of Mel[chi]zedek.

**2:10** [...over the]m [...] for

**2:11** that is the time of "the year of favor" for Melchizedek (Isa 61:2), and [of his] arm[ies,

**2:12** the nati]on of the holy ones of God, of the rule of judgment, as it is written

**2:13** concerning him in the psalms of David, who said: "God stands in the as[sembly of God];

**2:14** in the midst of the divine beings he judges" (Ps 82:1). And concerning him he said: "[Let the assembly of the peoples]

**2:15** return on high; and God on high will [j]udge the peoples" (Ps 7:8–9).

**2:16** As for what he sa[id: "How long will you] judge unjustly and sh[ow]

**2:17** partiality to the wicked? [Se]lah" (Ps 82:2).

**2:18** Its interpretation concerns Belial and the spirits of his lot, who [...]

**2:19** in their tur[ning] away from the commandments of God [to commit evil].

**2:20** And Melchizedek will exact the veng[eance] of the judgments of God [from the hand of Be]lial and from the hand of all the [spirits of] his [lot].

**2:21** And all the [eternal] divine beings are for his help. [This] is what [He said]:

**2:22** all the sons of Mi[ght and ...] the [a]ffair of Melchizedek.

**2:23** And [concerning what He said]: "How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messen[ger who]

**2:24** proclaims peace, the messen[ger of good who proclaims salva]tion, who says to Zion: 'Your God [reigns]'" (Isa 52:7).

**2:25** Its interpretation: the mountains are the pro[phets ...] the messenger is the anoin[ted of the Spir]it,

**2:26** about whom Dan[iel] said: ["Until an anointed one, a prince" (Dan 9:25) ...]

---

*SOPHIA notes: The consensus translation draws primarily from LOGOS for its formal clarity while incorporating EMET's precision on key terms and PNEUMA's readability where it improves understanding. This pesher text is among the most theologically significant Dead Sea Scrolls: it presents Melchizedek not as the priest-king of Genesis 14 but as a heavenly, eschatological figure who will execute divine judgment against Belial at the culmination of ten jubilees (490 years). The application of "Elohim" (Ps 82:1) directly to Melchizedek — rendered "God" in the consensus — reflects a remarkable divinization that has implications for understanding Second Temple angelology and early Christology. "Divine beings" (elohim/elim) in lines 14 and 21 distinguishes the members of the heavenly council. The jubilee chronology parallels Daniel 9:24–25's "seventy weeks of years." The anointed messenger of line 25–26 connects Isaiah 61, Isaiah 52:7, and Daniel 9:25 in a chain of prophetic fulfillment. Key disagreements involved the rendering of elohim (divine title vs. "divine beings"), "year of favor" vs. "year of grace," and the translation of pesher terminology — see disagreement log for full details.*
